answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to hold a distinct at-risk position: a copper stake exposed to real market movement, not a paper promise. When a thousand identities are one operator, their positions move together — one ripple in the market makes the portfolio rise and fall like a single pearl on a string. The network measures profit-and-loss correlation across identities and collapses any highly correlated cluster into one voice, so running a farm costs as much as running one honest agent, while genuine independents whose risks truly differ keep full standing.
